subject: [OT] fixed width font for code chunks

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: [OT] fixed width font for code chunks
parts:
Dear list,

(Apologies for being borderline off-topic)
I'm making a presentation in Beamer using knitr and xetex; I'm usually
happy with Inconsolata as a fixed width font for code chunks but I
noticed that some symbols, $ and <- in particular, can look quite ugly
because they have a wrong size / kerning in the context of R code. Do
you know a trick to special-case and fine-tune such characters? The
listing package can do some automatic replacements such as <- becoming
an arrow but I wonder if i) I can still use syntax highlighting based
on the parser, ii) copy+paste can work with such characters?

Thanks,

baptiste

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] [OT] fixed width font for code chunks
parts:
I think the relevant piece should be this:

\setbox\hlnormalsizeboxlessthan=\hbox{\begin{normalsize}\verb.<.\end{normalsize}}%
\setbox\hlnormalsizeboxdollar=\hbox{\begin{normalsize}\verb.$.\end{normalsize}}%

that is where <- and $ are defined by the highlight package. I'm not
familiar with \setbox, but I guess there might be a way like
\renewcommand to redefine these symbols... Another nasty trick is to
customize the 'source' hook; see render_latex (I replaced " with "{}
there, and you can also do other jobs there).

For listings, unfortunately you cannot copy the arrow, but you can
customize the definitions so that <- is not turned to a real arrow.

And just FYI (I'm off-topic too), HTML is so much more pleasing to
work with than the fragile LaTeX:
http://yihui.name/en/2012/04/fancy-html5-slides-with-knitr-and-pandoc/
I will release knitr 0.5 and write a tutorial hopefully tomorrow.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] [OT] fixed width font for code chunks
parts:
Hi Yihui,

It turns out that I was setting the chunk size with

\ifdefined\knitrout
\renewenvironment{knitrout}{\begin{footnotesize}}{\end{footnotesize}}
\else
\fi

but this doesn't affect the output of highlight() which is
'normalsize' by default. Setting size = 'footnotesize' as a global
option fixes the inconsistency and looks more natural.

Thanks,

baptiste
